The requirement in [requirement.feature](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_63_group_d_fix/requirement.feature) specifies that comparing two `NaN` double values for equality as well as comparing two double arrays containing `NaN` should evaluate to `false`.

### Cause & Fix
In [`MathUtils.equals(double x, double y)`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_63_group_d_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math/util/MathUtils.java#L416), the method was returning:
```java
(Double.isNaN(x) && Double.isNaN(y)) || x == y;
```
which evaluated to `true` when comparing two `NaN`s, violating the IEEE 754-compliant contract documented in its Javadoc (`equals(x, y, 1)`). Delegating to [`equals(x, y, 1)`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_63_group_d_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math/util/MathUtils.java#L476) ensures that `NaN` is not considered equal to `NaN`, correctly returning `false` for both scalar `NaN` comparisons and array equality checks.

The focused patch has been generated and saved to [enlightened_fix.patch](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_63_group_d_fix/enlightened_fix.patch).
